chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

He was asked about a man who has a sore on his forearm, or something like that, in a place of wudu (ablution), so he binds it with a cloth, performs wudu (ablution), and wipes over it when he performs wudu (ablution).
So he said: “If the water harms him, then let him wipe over the cloth; and if the water does not harm him, then let him remove the cloth and then wash it.”
He said: And I asked him about a wound—how should one deal with it in washing? He said: “Wash what is around it.”

key_terms.الْجُرْحِ: the wound requiring special handling in washing
key_terms.الْخِرْقَةِ: the cloth used to bind or cover the wound
key_terms.الْقَرْحَةُ: a sore or ulcer on the body
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, whose harm or lack of harm determines the ruling
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.ذِرَاعِهِ: his forearm, a limb involved in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.مَا حَوْلَهُ: what is around it, meaning the surrounding area of the wound
key_terms.يَمْسَحُ: he wipes, meaning passing the hand over a surface in ritual purification

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in wudu (ablution) or washing if there is a wound or sore on the limb?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on wudu (ablution) and washing when a person has a sore or wound on a limb. If water is harmful, one wipes over the cloth covering it; if it is not harmful, the covering is removed and the area is washed. For a wound in washing, the instruction is to wash around it.
